---
title: 9 - Info panel
---

You will add an information button that opens and closes a short description of the map. This panel can explain the map's purpose, data sources and important limitations.

Keep the text concise. A reader should be able to understand the map without needing to open a separate document.


## 9.1. Add the information button and panel

- [ ] Open `index.html`. 
- [ ] Inside the existing map container, add the block below to create an `info-button` and an `abstract-panel` that opens when the button is clicked. **Place this code after the title, on the same indentation level.** Do not remove the legend or other controls.

```html
      <!-- Abstract toggle via info-button -->
      <div class="map-info">

        <button
          id="info-button"
          class="info-button"
          type="button"
          aria-label="Show map abstract"
          aria-expanded="false"
          aria-controls="abstract-panel">
          i
        </button>

        <!-- Abstract panel that appears when toggled -->
        <div id="abstract-panel" class="abstract-panel" hidden>
          
          <h2> About this map</h2>

          <p>
            This webmap visualises the distribution of forest reserves, and national and international conservation areas in Tanzania. 
            International conservation areas consist of UNESCO World Heritage sites, as well as internationally important wetlands (Ramsar Sites).
          </p>

          <p>
            <strong>Data layers:</strong>
            Protected planet.
          </p>

          <p>
            <em>
              UNEP-WCMC (2026). Protected Area Profile for 
              United Republic of Tanzania from the World Database 
              on Protected Areas, September 2026. 
              Available at:
            </em>

            <a href="https://www.protectedplanet.net"
              target="_blank"
              rel="noopener noreferrer">
              www.protectedplanet.net
            </a>
          </p>

        </div>
      </div>
```

The abstract texts are very concise and simple in this example. For a real case, the description can be more detailed. An important element is the reference to the thematic data layers' provider.



## 9.2. Style the button and panel

- [ ] Open `style.css`.
- [ ] Add the following CSS to the end of the file:

```css
/* ----------------------------------------
    i-button and abstract panel
---------------------------------------- */
.map-info {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 70px;
  left: 10px;
  z-index: 1000;
}

.info-button {
  width: 36px;
  height: 36px;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: white;
  color: #333;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
  font-size: 20px;
  font-weight: bold;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.info-button:hover {
  background: #eeeeee;
}
```
The `.map-info` element positions the button and panel. The `hidden` attribute keeps the panel closed initially. In this example, the `info-button` and `map-title` overlap a bit. If you would like them not to, increase the `bottom` parameter of `.map.info { }` element to e.g. `85px`.

- [ ] Save `style.css`.


## 9.3. Make the button open and close the panel

Final step is to make the actual functionality of the `info-button` work. When the button is clicked, the abstract should appear.

- [ ] Open `main.js`.
- [ ] Add the code below at the end of the file, after the section where you configure the basemap toggle functionality:

```javascript
// Show or hide the map information panel (abstract)
const infoButton = document.getElementById("info-button");
const abstractPanel = document.getElementById("abstract-panel");

infoButton.addEventListener("click", () => {
  const isExpanded =
    infoButton.getAttribute("aria-expanded") === "true";

  abstractPanel.hidden = isExpanded;

  infoButton.setAttribute(
    "aria-expanded",
    String(!isExpanded)
  );

  infoButton.setAttribute(
    "aria-label",
    isExpanded ? "Show map abstract" : "Hide map abstract"
  );
});
```

This code checks whether the abstract panel is already open. If it is open, the click hides it; if it is closed, the click shows it. The `aria-expanded` and `aria-label` attributes help assistive technologies communicate the button's state and purpose.

- [ ] Save `main.js` and refresh the map.
- [ ] Test the info-button functionality.


**[SCREENSHOT 9.1: Show the information panel open with its button, title and legend visible. Use realistic, final text rather than placeholder text.]**

::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint

- [ ] The abstract panel is hidden when the map first opens.
- [ ] The information button opens and closes it.
- [ ] The panel remains readable on a smaller screen.
- [ ] The text identifies the map's subject and credits its data source.
:::
